newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Shell Berre refinery workers extend strike.
newsitem.headline: French Shell Berre refinery workers extend strike.

text.p: French oil workers at Royal Dutch/Shell's Berre refinery near Marseille extended a strike begun on Monday for another 24 hours from Tuesday morning, a Shell official at the plant said.
The official said crude distillation was being suspended after workers extended their strike during a shift change at 0300 GMT. Distillation had previously continued at a slow rate.
An employee at the nearby BP Lavera refinery said a scheduled one-day strike there had gone ahead on Tuesday, but there was no immediate management or union confirmation.
The Berre official said crude distillation was in the process of being halted, but the distillation tower would continue to recycle product and could be restarted quickly.
"It's in the process of being stopped now and it would take us about half a day to get it going again," he said.
Catalytic cracking at the 128,000 barrels per day refinery continued at a slower than normal rate, he said.
Most chemical units were shut including the steam cracker used to make ethylene. Chemical units can be brought in and out of service more easily than complex conversion units for oil.
Unions have given advance notice on Monday that they would extend a 24-hour strike at Berre for another day until early Wednesday.
The action coincides with union calls for a nationwide oil industry strike on Tuesday, though only three plants including Berre and Lavera are expected to be hit directly.
Unions said Total's 130,000 bpd La Mede refinery near Marseille would be on strike from 1100 GMT on Tuesday.
Unions also planned a go-slow at Shell's 140,000 bpd Petit Couronne refinery in northern France but there was no immediate word on the refinery's status on Tuesday morning.
